unit.villager.name: Villager
unit.villager.desc: A civilian worker who gathers resources and constructs buildings. The backbone of your economy.
unit.scout.name: Scout
unit.scout.desc: A fast-moving unit that explores the map and reveals enemy positions. Weak in combat.
unit.spearman.name: Spearman
unit.spearman.desc: A light infantry unit armed with a long spear. Effective against cavalry units.
unit.archer.name: Archer
unit.archer.desc: A ranged unit that attacks from a distance. Vulnerable to cavalry charges.
unit.man-at-arms.name: Man-at-Arms
unit.man-at-arms.desc: A professional soldier clad in medium armor. Well-rounded and reliable in most engagements.
unit.knight.name: Knight
unit.knight.desc: A heavily armored cavalry unit. Powerful in charges but expensive to field and maintain.
unit.crossbowman.name: Crossbowman
unit.crossbowman.desc: A ranged unit with a powerful crossbow. Slower attack speed but greater armor penetration.
unit.horseman.name: Horseman
unit.horseman.desc: A fast cavalry unit ideal for raiding and flanking enemy formations.
unit.handcannoneer.name: Hand Cannoneer
unit.handcannoneer.desc: A gunpowder unit with devastating ranged attack. Particularly effective against heavily armored foes.
unit.siege-ram.name: Siege Ram
unit.siege-ram.desc: A massive battering ram designed to demolish enemy fortifications and buildings.
unit.mangonel.name: Mangonel
unit.mangonel.desc: A stone-throwing siege engine that deals area-of-effect damage. Devastating against infantry formations.
unit.trebuchet.name: Trebuchet
unit.trebuchet.desc: A long-range counterweight siege engine. Highly effective against buildings but immobile when firing.
unit.longbowman.name: Longbowman
unit.longbowman.desc: An elite English archer with exceptional range and rate of fire. A symbol of English military might.
unit.royal-knight.name: Royal Knight
unit.royal-knight.desc: A prestigious French cavalry unit with a powerful charge ability that deals bonus damage on the first strike.
unit.landsknecht.name: Landsknecht
unit.landsknecht.desc: A feared Holy Roman Empire mercenary swordsman who deals bonus damage against groups of infantry.
unit.mangudai.name: Mangudai
unit.mangudai.desc: An elite Mongol horse archer capable of shooting while moving at full speed.
unit.fire-lancer.name: Fire Lancer
unit.fire-lancer.desc: A Chinese cavalry unit that ignites enemies on charge, dealing ongoing fire damage.
unit.zhuge-nu.name: Zhuge Nu
unit.zhuge-nu.desc: A Chinese crossbowman armed with a repeating crossbow, firing multiple bolts in rapid succession.
unit.war-elephant.name: War Elephant
unit.war-elephant.desc: A massive Delhi Sultanate war beast that tramples enemies and terrifies nearby foes.
unit.streltsy.name: Streltsy
unit.streltsy.desc: A Russian musketeer who excels in melee combat after firing, blending gunpowder and close-quarters fighting.
unit.boyar.name: Boyar
unit.boyar.desc: A Russian heavy cavalry unit with exceptional armor and resilience in sustained combat.
unit.janissary.name: Janissary
unit.janissary.desc: An elite Ottoman infantry unit armed with a musket. A disciplined and powerful fighting force.
unit.great-bombard.name: Great Bombard
unit.great-bombard.desc: The Ottoman empire's fearsome heavy cannon, capable of destroying walls and fortifications with ease.
unit.musofaba.name: Musofaba
unit.musofaba.desc: A Mali scout and skirmisher, swift and effective at harassing enemy supply lines.
unit.donso.name: Donso
unit.donso.desc: A Mali hunter-warrior who excels in woodlands and gains bonuses when near forest terrain.
unit.camel-rider.name: Camel Rider
unit.camel-rider.desc: An Abbasid cavalry unit mounted on a camel. The scent of camels disrupts enemy horses, reducing their combat effectiveness.
unit.camel-archer.name: Camel Archer
unit.camel-archer.desc: A fast ranged cavalry unit mounted on a camel, combining mobility with harassment firepower.
unit.keshik.name: Keshik
unit.keshik.desc: An elite Mongol cavalry unit that generates resources while fighting, fueling the Mongol war machine.
unit.arbaletrier.name: Arbaletrier
unit.arbaletrier.desc: A French elite crossbowman with a pavise shield, capable of setting up a defensive position for sustained fire.
building.town-center.name: Town Center
building.town-center.desc: The heart of your civilization. Train villagers, research technologies, and advance through the ages.
building.house.name: House
building.house.desc: Provides additional population capacity. Build more houses to support a larger army.
building.barracks.name: Barracks
building.barracks.desc: Trains infantry units including spearmen and men-at-arms.
building.archery-range.name: Archery Range
building.archery-range.desc: Trains ranged units such as archers and crossbowmen.
building.stable.name: Stable
building.stable.desc: Trains cavalry units including horsemen and knights.
building.blacksmith.name: Blacksmith
building.blacksmith.desc: Researches weapon and armor upgrades for your military units.
building.mill.name: Mill
building.mill.desc: A drop-off point for food. Research improvements to farming efficiency.
building.farm.name: Farm
building.farm.desc: A renewable source of food. Villagers work the land to produce sustenance for your people.
building.lumber-camp.name: Lumber Camp
building.lumber-camp.desc: A drop-off point for wood. Research improvements to wood gathering.
building.mining-camp.name: Mining Camp
building.mining-camp.desc: A drop-off point for gold and stone. Research improvements to mining efficiency.
building.market.name: Market
building.market.desc: Exchange resources and send trade caravans to allied markets for steady gold income.
building.dock.name: Dock
building.dock.desc: Builds and repairs ships. Essential for naval supremacy and fishing operations.
building.keep.name: Keep
building.keep.desc: A powerful defensive tower with large garrison capacity and strong attack. The cornerstone of medieval defense.
building.tower.name: Outpost Tower
building.tower.desc: A defensive structure that provides vision and attacks nearby enemies. Garrison units for increased firepower.
building.wall-stone.name: Stone Wall
building.wall-stone.desc: A thick fortification that denies enemy passage and absorbs heavy punishment.
building.wall-wood.name: Palisade Wall
building.wall-wood.desc: A quick wooden barrier to block enemy movement in the early game.
building.gate.name: Gate
building.gate.desc: A fortified gate that allows your units to pass while blocking enemies.
building.siege-workshop.name: Siege Workshop
building.siege-workshop.desc: Constructs powerful siege engines including mangonels, rams, and trebuchets.
building.university.name: University
building.university.desc: Researches advanced technologies to improve your civilization's military and economic capabilities.
building.monastery.name: Monastery
building.monastery.desc: Trains monks who can convert enemy units and heal friendly forces.
civ.english.name: English
civ.english.desc: Masters of ranged warfare. The English longbowman is among the most feared projectile units in the world. Their farming economy is the most efficient, and their network of keeps projects power across the map.
civ.french.name: French
civ.french.desc: A wealthy and powerful civilization that excels in cavalry and economic growth. The French can trade at a discount and field the devastating Royal Knight.
civ.hre.name: Holy Roman Empire
civ.hre.desc: A faith-driven civilization with powerful religious bonuses. Their relics provide lasting economic advantages, and the Prelate inspires workers to gather faster.
civ.mongols.name: Mongols
civ.mongols.desc: A nomadic superpower with unmatched mobility. Mongol armies can relocate their entire base and field elite horse archers that generate resources in combat.
civ.chinese.name: Chinese
civ.chinese.desc: An innovative and resilient civilization with powerful gunpowder units and a dynasty system that unlocks unique bonuses as the game progresses.
civ.delhi.name: Delhi Sultanate
civ.delhi.desc: A scholarly civilization that researches technologies for free using scholars. They field the terrifying War Elephant and boast some of the strongest defensive structures.
civ.rus.name: Rus
civ.rus.desc: A hunter civilization that thrives in the wilderness. Hunting animals generates gold, and their distinctive wooden architecture gives them a strong early economy.
civ.abbasid.name: Abbasid Dynasty
civ.abbasid.desc: A culture-focused civilization that builds a wondrous House of Wisdom to unlock powerful wings of technologies. They excel in camel cavalry and economic flexibility.
civ.ottoman.name: Ottoman Empire
civ.ottoman.desc: A militaristic empire with a powerful standing army. The Ottomans field the elite Janissary and the devastating Great Bombard, making them nearly unstoppable on the battlefield.
civ.mali.name: Mali
civ.mali.desc: A gold-rich civilization from West Africa. The Mali use a unique Pit Mine to generate infinite gold and field distinctive infantry hunters who thrive in forested terrain.
resource.food.name: Food
resource.food.desc: Used to train most military units and villagers. Gathered from farms, hunting, and fishing.
resource.wood.name: Wood
resource.wood.desc: Used to construct buildings and train certain units. Gathered from trees.
resource.gold.name: Gold
resource.gold.desc: A precious resource used for advanced units and technologies. Gathered from gold mines or trade.
resource.stone.name: Stone
resource.stone.desc: Used for advanced defensive structures and certain buildings. Gathered from stone deposits.
resource.influence.name: Influence
resource.influence.desc: A special resource that represents political and cultural power. Used for unique civilization abilities.
resource.population.name: Population
resource.population.desc: The number of units you can field. Increased by building houses and other population-providing structures.
age.age1.name: Dark Age
age.age1.desc: The starting age. Basic economic and military units are available.
age.age2.name: Feudal Age
age.age2.desc: The second age. Access to more military units and economic buildings.
age.age3.name: Castle Age
age.age3.desc: The third age. Powerful military units and fortifications become available.
age.age4.name: Imperial Age
age.age4.desc: The final age. Access to the most powerful units, technologies, and wonders.

guide.title: GUIDE
guide.step1: Select your villagers (drag a box around them) and right-click a tree, berry bush or sheep to gather.
guide.step2: Train more villagers: select the Town Center and use the production buttons. Keep it producing.
guide.step3: Build a House or Farm: select a villager, pick a building from the menu and click to place it.
guide.step4: Gather enough food and gold, then advance to the Feudal Age from the Town Center.
guide.step5: Well done! Build barracks, train an army and destroy the enemy landmarks to win. (Click to dismiss)
